hardware.note: Findings about the F(x)tec Pro¹x (QX1050, SM6115) that hold under any OS, seen while porting Guix System. Only what this port measured or had to solve; the much larger hardware corpus for this phone is moWerk's sailfish-rag Mainline/ (read-only reference, see README). Seeded 2026-10-28 from this repository's git history and TODO.md; entries labelled handover were not re-checked on the device.

boot_chain.title: U-Boot's bootmenu can show a menu at every boot through the environment alone
boot_chain.general: On qcom phone builds, bootretry=1 ends an extlinux menu at once, since endtime is unset before bootcmd. bootmenu has its own loop: bootmenu N counts down, bootmenu -1 waits for a key. env import -t in preboot can load labels and the delay from a file on disk, so they change without a reflash.
boot_chain.instance: Pro¹x, U-Boot environment in packages/uboot.scm, labels from /boot/extlinux/menu.env. Author's test with -1: menu waits, keys work, a previous entry boots; with 15, the countdown worked and the default entry booted (author's test).

boot_chain.title: Qualcomm ABL rejects a U-Boot arm64 Image whose header text_offset is not zero
boot_chain.general: The Qualcomm Android bootloader (ABL) checks the arm64 Image header of the kernel in the boot image. A U-Boot binary built with a negative text_offset (bytes 8-15 of the header) is refused and the phone falls straight back to fastboot, with no message. Zero text_offset as Linux does, gzip the image, and append the DTB after the gzip stream so ABL hands it to U-Boot in x0.
boot_chain.instance: Pro¹x, U-Boot packed as an Android boot image in boot_a/boot_b by scripts/flash.sh. U-Boot's header had text_offset = -0x80000000. The NixOS port already did this; the Guix flash script had missed it. --second was dropped once the DTB was appended.

boot_chain.title: AVB vbmeta flags are at byte offset 120 of the header
boot_chain.general: To disable verification with a hand-made vbmeta image, the flags word (value 3: verification and hashtree disabled) goes at byte offset 120 of vbmeta_image_header_t, and the image is zero-padded to 4096 bytes. Writing it anywhere else leaves verification enabled, and ABL rejects the unsigned boot image by falling back to fastboot.
boot_chain.instance: scripts/flash.sh first wrote the flag at offset 48 (the signature_offset field). Fixed by building the header with Python struct.pack_into so the offset is explicit (scripts/mkvbmeta.py).

boot_chain.title: Flash U-Boot to both boot slots and set slot A active
boot_chain.general: On an A/B Qualcomm phone, if only one boot slot holds the new bootloader, a failed boot can make ABL switch to the other slot and boot the old stock image, or loop between slots. Flashing both slots avoids the loop, but it leaves no stock slot to fall back to: the only way back to Android is a reflash.
boot_chain.instance: scripts/flash.sh flashes boot_a, boot_b, vbmeta_a and vbmeta_b, erases dtbo, flashes userdata, then runs set_active a. The README still says 'replaces the bootloader on slot A' only (as of 018fa97).

boot_chain.title: A one-shot boot entry with a known-good default makes kernel experiments recoverable without hands
boot_chain.general: With U-Boot and extlinux, boot the system under test through a one-shot entry while the default stays a known-good system, so any crash or hang comes back to something reachable over ssh after a reset. Without it, a kernel or initrd that does not boot needs a person at the boot menu.
boot_chain.instance: moWerk's SailfishOS port keeps NixOS as the default on userdata and enters SailfishOS through a one-shot extlinux entry. This Guix port has no such mechanism yet: recovery is the volume-down boot menu with previous generations (TODO.md section 11).

boot_chain.title: U-Boot extlinux refuses kernel command lines over 511 bytes (CONFIG_SYS_CBSIZE=512 in qcom_defconfig)
boot_chain.general: U-Boot builds bootargs for an extlinux/PXE label in a CONFIG_SYS_CBSIZE buffer; a longer APPEND prints "bootarg overflow" and the label does not boot. qcom_defconfig sets 512. Long store paths (gnu.system, gnu.load) already take about half of it on Guix; options like vt.default_red/grn/blu push it over. Raise CONFIG_SYS_CBSIZE or keep the command line short.
boot_chain.instance: Pro¹x, U-Boot 2026.10-rc f8eb346: generations 22-24 with the three vt.default_* arguments (APPEND 569 bytes) did not boot; the phone came up from prev3 (generation 21, 284 bytes). The palette moved back to setvtrgb at boot. Generation 25: 317 bytes.
boot_chain.source: boot/pxe_utils.c label_boot (bootargs[CONFIG_SYS_CBSIZE]), configs/qcom_defconfig in the u-boot-pro1x source; /proc/cmdline on the phone (gnu.system=system-21-link); APPEND lengths in /boot/extlinux/prev*.conf

kernel.title: QRTR name service and PD mapper are in the kernel config; no userspace daemons needed for them
kernel.general: Recent kernels provide the QRTR name service and the protection domain mapper in-kernel (CONFIG_QRTR, CONFIG_QCOM_PD_MAPPER). Guides that list qrtr-ns and pd-mapper daemons are outdated. rmtfs and tqftpserv are still needed.
kernel.instance: CONFIG_QRTR=y and CONFIG_QCOM_PD_MAPPER=y in device/kernel/config.aarch64. rmtfs, tqftpserv and pro1x-hexagonrpcd run as Shepherd services (seen running on the 2026-10-27 flash, per TODO.md).
kernel.source: device/kernel/config.aarch64 lines 1645 and 9530 at 018fa97, read in source; sailfish-rag Mainline/firmware_remoteproc.json

kernel.title: Enable zstd firmware decompression when the firmware package ships .zst files
kernel.general: If the distribution compresses firmware files, the kernel firmware loader needs the matching option (CONFIG_FW_LOADER_COMPRESS_ZSTD or _XZ), or every request_firmware fails as 'file not found' although the file is there.
kernel.instance: Enabled in device/kernel/config.aarch64 for the Guix build. The reason (linux-firmware from nonguix shipping .zst files) is not written in the commit.
kernel.source: commits a60b1f2, d58b891; confirm with: ls $(guix build linux-firmware)/lib/firmware/qcom | head

kernel.title: s2idle: the Bluetooth UART wakes the SoC at once
kernel.general: On Qualcomm phones with a UART-attached Bluetooth chip, the UART RX wake IRQ can end every s2idle within seconds; disable that device's power/wakeup while suspended (Bluetooth keeps working).
kernel.instance: Pro1X, Linux 7.1 sm6115-mainline: woke after 2.2 s on IRQ 110 4a8c000.serial:wakeup (/sys/power/pm_wakeup_irq); with /sys/devices/platform/soc@0/4ac0000.geniqup/4a8c000.serial/power/wakeup disabled it slept until the power key (IRQ pm8941_pwrkey) or the RTC alarm (pm8xxx_rtc_alarm).
kernel.source: device/sway/pro1x-sleep; suspend tests on the phone 2026-11-01

kernel.title: s2idle: the ADSP sensor process crashes at resume (fastrpc resends the frozen listener call)
kernel.general: With hexagonrpcd serving the ADSP sensor PD, the freezer interrupts its listener ioctl (-ERESTARTSYS) and mainline fastrpc sends the restarted call again; the duplicate crashes sensor_process in frpc_dsp at resume. Stopping only the sensor clients does not help. Fix in the kernel: resume the interrupted context (downstream context_restore_interrupted) and take a wakeup event per DSP message.
kernel.instance: Pro1X 7.1: PDM: service sensor_process crash EX:sensor_process:0x1:frpc_dsp:0xc0 at every resume; ADSP recovery (debugfs recover) then brought sensors back but not the sound card (wcd937x_codec ASoC error -16, snd-sm8250 failed -16; the codec cannot be unbound: Permission denied), so no sound until reboot. Same crash and cause on the Lenovo TB-J606L (SM6115); its patches 0015/0016 carried as pro1x-fastrpc-wake / pro1x-fastrpc-resume-interrupted (0016 adapted to 7.1). postmarketOS google-sargo stops hexagonrpcd before suspend instead.
kernel.source: github.com/haltia-de/device-lenovo-tb-j606l issues/23, pull/12, kernel/patches; pmaports MR 5400; crash and audio loss confirmed on the Pro1X; the fix not yet booted

kernel.title: s2idle: modem messages do not wake user space (GLINK SMEM is IRQF_NO_SUSPEND without a wakeup event)
kernel.general: qcom_glink_smem requests its IRQ IRQF_NO_SUSPEND and reports no wakeup event, so an incoming call is received by the kernel in s2idle while ModemManager stays frozen. smp2p is wakeup-capable but off by default and carries no QMI messages.
kernel.instance: Pro1X 7.1, drivers/rpmsg/qcom_glink_smem.c line 308; our patch pro1x-glink-modem-wake takes a wakeup event on the mpss edge; /sys/devices/platform/smp2p-mpss/power/wakeup disabled. Kernel v3 (2026-11-01): wakeup only for QRTR data to user-space sockets (af_qrtr, sk_kern_sock false), switch /sys/module/qrtr/parameters/wake_on_data; v1 (every GLINK message) and v2 (every QRTR data packet) aborted each suspend: 2-4 packets of 48 bytes 0.2-0.4 s after each entry. With v3 an RTC-woken suspend held 45 s, woken by the RTC only, ADSP and sound intact. Wake on an incoming call not yet tested.
kernel.source: kernel source read; patch not yet booted

kernel.title: s2idle does not reach SoC deep sleep: qcom_stats vlow and vmin stay at 0
kernel.general: On SM6115 mainline, a held s2idle only idles the CPUs (psci per-core power collapse); the RPM low-power modes vlow/vmin need every master (modem, ADSP, CDSP, WCN) to vote for sleep and XO to be released. Check /sys/kernel/debug/qcom_stats/{vlow,vmin} Count before trusting a suspend drain figure.
kernel.instance: Pro1X 7.1: psci_idle driver, states WFI and cpu-sleep-0-0 / cpu-sleep-1-0 used; vlow and vmin Count 0 after suspends of 11 s and more (2026-11-01). moWerk measures 47.5 mA in suspend on SailfishOS (7.3) and suspects the same; the TB-J606L port (SM6115) reports vlow/vmin at 0 with XO votes as its next step.
kernel.source: qcom_stats and cpuidle sysfs on the phone; moWerk (message to the author); github.com/haltia-de/device-lenovo-tb-j606l pull/12

modem.title: ModemManager needs udev tags on rmnet_ipa0 to pair the IPA data port with the QRTR control port
modem.general: With ModemManager's qcom-soc plugin, the IPA network interface must carry ID_MM_CANDIDATE=1 and ID_MM_PHYSDEV_UID=qcom-soc, or MM never associates it with the modem found over QRTR and mobile data cannot come up. The IPA driver can register the interface before the rule is loaded, so re-trigger udev (udevadm trigger, settle) before starting MM. ModemManager ships these tags itself in 77-mm-qcom-soc.rules (DRIVERS==ipa or bam-dmux), so installing MM's udev rules is enough; a device rule is a fallback.
modem.instance: Image 6b37ac4, 2026-10-28: MM 1.24.0 probes qrtr0, then "couldn't create modem for device 'qcom-soc': Failed to find a net port in the QMI modem". udevadm info on rmnet_ipa0 showed no ID_MM_* property at all: neither device/udev/60-pro1x.rules nor MM's own 77-mm-qcom-soc.rules (which tags DRIVERS=="ipa" net ports with ID_MM_PHYSDEV_UID=qcom-soc) was loaded (see guix.json, udev extensions). The rule text is right; the Guix wiring was wrong. Fixed, not yet re-tested.

modem.title: Build ModemManager for QMI over QRTR only: MBIM is not needed on SoC modems
modem.general: Qualcomm SoC modems are reached over QRTR with QMI, not MBIM. If the distribution's libmbim is too old for a newer ModemManager, disable MBIM support rather than packaging a new libmbim.
modem.instance: modem-manager 1.24 built without MBIM (needs libmbim >= 1.32) and with the qcom-soc plugin forced on.

modem.title: A voice-centric modem setting can keep a phone off LTE without VoLTE
modem.general: 3GPP lets a voice-centric UE that cannot do voice on LTE (no IMS/VoLTE, no CSFB from the operator) leave E-UTRAN. On a mainline port without IMS, check the modem's usage preference before blaming bands or carrier profiles.
modem.instance: Pro1X: 4G allowed and preferred, every LTE band enabled, carrier profile ROW_Commercial (the only generic one of 25: Asian, Brazilian, Russian operators), yet UMTS only, 28% signal; another phone gets 5G at the same place. qmicli --nas-get-system-selection-preference: usage voice-centric, voice ps-preferred. Not tested: data-centric is stored in modem NV (modemst via rmtfs), author's decision pending. moWerk's notes: LTE registered on this phone with another operator.

modem.title: GNSS: LOC service present, but no NMEA
modem.general: A QMI LOC service on QRTR does not prove the GNSS engine works; check that NMEA indications arrive before writing a location stack.
modem.instance: Pro1X, 2026-10-30: QMI service 16 (LOC v2) on QRTR; ModemManager lists gps-raw, gps-nmea, agps-msa/msb. SUPL server and agps-msb fail ('Failed to receive indication'); gps-nmea enabled but 'couldn't setup required NMEA traces: Operation timed out'; qmicli --loc-follow-nmea for 75 s: nothing; 30+ min indoors: nothing. No port has GPS on this phone (NixOS README: untested; moWerk: not started).
modem.source: ModemManager log and qmicli on the phone

modem.title: QMI data bearers are multiplexed; a second context may still be refused by the network
modem.general: ModemManager on QMI/rmnet multiplexes bearers (qmapmux links), so two data contexts are possible on the modem side. Whether the network accepts a second PDP context on another APN is the operator's decision; 3GPP cause 33 (option unsubscribed) is the network refusing, not a modem fault. A second bearer without its own 3GPP profile can fail with 'call-already-present' (same profile slot). Snapshot the 3GPP profile list before adding one, and compare after deleting it.
modem.instance: Pro1X, 2026-10-30: data bearer on qmapmux0.0; a second bearer created qmapmux0.1 (mux id 2); with a dedicated profile (IPv4) the network answered cause 33. The profile was deleted and the list compared with the snapshot: identical. Earlier refusals came from a mistyped APN.
modem.source: ModemManager log and mmcli on the phone

modem.title: Check the operator's published APN before assuming a separate MMS APN
modem.general: Many operators carry MMS on the data APN (APN type default,mms). A separate MMS APN entered by mistake makes every MMS download fail; with the combined APN, mmsd-tng fetches over the data connection. Restart mmsd-tng after changing its settings so it processes its queue again.
modem.instance: Pro1X with the author's operator: combined APN; after correcting the MMS APN and a proxy port typo (89 for 80) the four waiting MMS downloaded at once.

modem.title: A missed call on LTE can coincide with a network rejection, and is not a kernel matter
modem.general: Before blaming a kernel for calls going to voicemail on LTE, match call events against ModemManager's rejections and radio type: the same kernel can ring on LTE minutes earlier. Repeated EMM rejections and detaches leave moments in which a call is lost.
modem.instance: Pro1x, Free SIM (208-15), 2026-11-05, kernel 7.3.0, generation 219: rang at 09:12:45 with LTE system info 7 s before and LTE after. At 09:13:51 a call appeared in ModemManager as unknown -> terminated in the same second as rejection 'ms-identity-not-derived-by-network' (9), 'no-cells-in-location-area' (15) and bearer end emm-detached. Causes 9 and 15 are logged on every day from 2026-10-30, with 7.1 too. This replaces the earlier notes' 'on 7.3 4G does not ring' and the QRTR lead, which had no evidence. Which of the author's call attempts is which event is not established; why the network rejects, and whether Android on this SIM behaves the same, is not known.
modem.confidence: confirmed (timings, one ring and one lost call), inferred (rejection causes the loss)
modem.source: /var/log/messages on the phone, ModemManager lines; author's test calls

modem.title: Incoming calls on LTE: about one in three rings, whatever the voice domain or a busy data link
modem.general: A phone without VoLTE on an LTE network receives calls by CS fallback: the network moves it to 2G/3G for the call. Count rings against calls with the caller reporting each result, and log the radio beside them. A voicemail with no radio change leaves no trace on the phone, so the phone cannot detect it. Poll the modem directly as well: ModemManager 1.24 logs 'unexpected LTE system info: domain camped' and reports searching and packet-detached while QMI serving system says registered, CS and PS attached.
modem.instance: Pro1X, 7.3.0, generations 229-232, SIM home 20815, 2026-11-05. Starting on Free LTE. Voice domain ps-preferred, no ping: rang 1 of 3 (first round), 2 of 5 (second round: 2 voicemails with no radio change, 1 with a move to 3G and no ring). cs-preferred, until power cycle: 2 of 5 by the author's count, 1 ring in ModemManager's log. ps-preferred with 49 pings/s on the data link: 1 of 3 (1 voicemail with no radio change, 1 with a move to 3G and no ring). Orange 20801 3G: 6 of 6 rang. Neither setting nor a busy link changed the result visibly, on small samples. Each ring came with a move to 3G. Reject cause 9 on PS and a dropped bearer follow most returns to LTE; a call rang 16 s after one, so it does not block calls by itself. Bouygues refuses the SIM with cause 11, SFR with 13. A return to LTE took from seconds to 10 min. 7.1 not yet compared with this test. Ping traffic: 2.5 kB/s measured on qmapmux0.0, about 9 MB/h.
modem.confidence: confirmed for the counts and logs; the cause is not known
modem.source: /root/call-test/net.log and cs.log on the phone, /var/log/messages, author's report per call

usb_network.title: Keep the phone's DHCP server from handing the host a default route
usb_network.general: When the phone serves DHCP on the USB gadget interface, it must not advertise a router (DHCP option 3), or the host replaces its own default route with the phone and loses its network.
usb_network.instance: dnsmasq in usb-network.scm started with --dhcp-option=3 (empty), phone at 172.16.42.1.

storage_and_fde.title: Passphrase prompt on the phone: console, keyboard and timing
storage_and_fde.general: A generation whose initrd tries small LUKS files on a plain root tests the prompt, keyboard and Argon2 cost without wiping anything. The initrd's static Guile has no ioctl symbol and no udev or losetup: find the partition through /sys/class/block/*/uevent PARTNAME and set up the loop with a small static program. cryptsetup 2.8 aborts on --tries 0.
storage_and_fde.instance: Pro¹x, generations 212-213: readable in landscape, letters and digits right without Fn, no echo; partition found at 2.4 s; Argon2id 256 MiB, 4 passes, unlock 8 s including typing 10 digits. Real layout on UFS not flashed yet.

storage_and_fde.title: cryptsetup cannot open LUKS2 at an offset; use a loop device with losetup -o
storage_and_fde.general: cryptsetup's --offset applies to plain and loop-AES mappings, not LUKS2. To place a LUKS2 container after an unencrypted region on the same partition, expose the region with losetup -o <bytes> and open LUKS2 on the loop device. The kernel needs CONFIG_BLK_DEV_LOOP=y if this happens in the initrd.
storage_and_fde.instance: userdata keeps a 256 MiB plain area (boot files for U-Boot) followed by LUKS2. fxtec-pro1x/services/fde.scm. FDE as a whole is untested on the device.

storage_and_fde.title: Grow the root filesystem to the partition on first boot by comparing sizes, not with a flag alone
storage_and_fde.general: A rootfs image smaller than userdata needs resize2fs on the device. Comparing the partition size with the filesystem size (as Droidian does) is idempotent and survives reflashes; a flag file alone can skip a needed resize.
storage_and_fde.instance: pro1x-rootfs-resize-service-type in fxtec-pro1x/services/boot.scm; seen to run on the 2026-10-27 flash.

wifi.title: Wi-Fi (ath10k_snoc) works once tqftpserv serves the firmware over QRTR
wifi.general: On SM6115 the WCN3990 Wi-Fi firmware is loaded by the modem DSP through tqftpserv, so Wi-Fi depends on the modem remoteproc and tqftpserv finding the firmware files.
wifi.instance: ath10k_snoc driver, NetworkManager connected with IPv4 and IPv6 on home Wi-Fi, after the tqftpserv firmware path fix (see guix.json).

display.title: Ghost touches came from the panel running at 61 Hz: set the DSI pixel clock for exactly 60 Hz
display.general: A touch controller can pick up the display scan as touches when the panel refresh rate is off from what the stock firmware uses. Phantom touch events that appear only while the panel is on point at the display mode (pixel clock, porches), not at the touch driver. Compute the refresh rate as clock / (htotal * vtotal) and match the stock fps.
display.instance: BOE BF060Y8M-AJ0 panel (drivers/gpu/drm/panel/panel-boe-bf060y8m-aj0.c), 1236 x 2192 total. Mainline .clock = 165268 kHz gives 61.00 Hz and about 5000 phantom touch events per 10 s with the panel on; 162559 kHz gives 60.00 Hz and none. The fix is in device/kernel/patches/pro1x-dsi.patch, applied by fxtec-pro1x/packages/kernel.scm since the first commit 5ad022d. Arithmetic checked; not yet observed on this port with getevent/libinput.
display.source: nyymi (NixOS port author), message relayed by the author on 2026-10-28; device/kernel/patches/pro1x-dsi.patch lines 9-15

display.title: Reading the panel backlight (actual_brightness) wedges the DSI link; the panel fades to white
display.general: On a DSI panel whose backlight is controlled over DCS, reading actual_brightness makes the driver issue a DCS read (set max return packet size 0x37, then read). In video mode on this SoC that read times out; repeated polling (a status bar block) left the DSI host unable to send even writes, and the AMOLED panel slowly turned fully white. Power-cycling the output through the compositor did not recover it; a reboot did. Do not poll actual_brightness on such panels; reading brightness (the cached value) or writing it is the safe path, but check with dmesg.
display.instance: panel-sw43404-boe-fhd-amoled on 5e94000.dsi, image 6b37ac4, kernel 7.1.0. i3status-rust backlight block on /sys/class/backlight/5e94000.dsi.0, run by hand twice at 19:29 UTC: dmesg from 8604 s on "dsi_cmds2buf_tx: cmd dma tx failed, type=0x37 ... ret=-110", "wait for video done timed out"; later "sending DCS SET_DISPLAY_OFF failed: -110". Panel white; reboot needed. Block removed from device/sway/i3status-rust.toml.
display.source: phone dmesg 2026-10-28; author observed the white panel

display.title: The Adreno 610 renders: check devfreq before assuming software rendering
display.general: Mesa's libgallium holds the GPU driver and llvmpipe, and libLLVM is mapped either way, so the loaded libraries prove nothing. The GPU's devfreq trans_stat shows whether it works.
display.instance: Pro1X, phoc 0.56: /sys/class/devfreq/5900000.gpu, 17473 transitions and about 6 min at 950 MHz in one boot: freedreno in use. card0 and renderD128 are msm_dpu.

display.title: The keyboard slide is SW_KEYPAD_SLIDE on gpio-keys; Phosh ignores it
display.general: Compositors and shells handle lid and tablet switches, rarely the keypad-slide switch; a phone with a sliding keyboard needs its own watcher for rotation and backlight.
display.instance: Pro1X: gpio-keys (also volume-up, camera), udev symlink /dev/input/pro1x-slider. Phosh rotated with the sensor with the keyboard out; a session helper locks rotation and sets transform 270 on slide-out (90, as in Sway's config, was upside down in Phosh).

video.title: GPU rendering is hardware-accelerated (Mesa gallium on Adreno 610); no hardware video codec yet
video.general: Check GPU acceleration from the compositor side: which Mesa libraries the compositor maps (/proc/PID/maps) and whether the GPU devfreq leaves its idle frequency under load (/sys/class/devfreq/*gpu*/trans_stat). Qualcomm video decode/encode is Venus/Iris, a V4L2 memory-to-memory device: VA-API (libva) has no driver for it; users are FFmpeg *_v4l2m2m codecs (mpv --hwdec=v4l2m2m-copy) and GStreamer v4l2 elements. Browsers that only speak VA-API get no video acceleration.
video.instance: Image 6b37ac4, kernel 7.1.0 (sm6115-mainline 8cd9520): sway maps libgallium-26.0.2.so and dri_gbm.so; GPU devfreq moved 320 -> 745/950 MHz 535 times while sway ran. Renderer string not read (eglinfo not installed). No Venus: only camss /dev/video*, no venus module loaded, although CONFIG_VIDEO_QCOM_VENUS=m and CONFIG_VIDEO_QCOM_IRIS=m.

video.title: Venus on SM6115: firmware present, driver support present via QCM2290 (AR50 Lite), device-tree node missing
video.general: SM6115 shares the AR50 Lite video core with QCM2290 (Agatti). With the qcm2290-venus support in the driver, enabling Venus is mostly a device-tree node in sm6115.dtsi modelled on agatti.dtsi, plus a compatible (sm6115 or reuse of qcm2290) accepted by the driver and binding. Register base, interrupt, IOMMU stream IDs and OPPs must be checked against SM6115 (downstream bengal DT), not assumed from Agatti.
video.instance: Kernel tree 8cd9520: venus/core.c matches qcom,qcm2290-venus but no sm6115; sm6115.dtsi has no video-codec node but has pil_video_mem at 0x51400000 (0x500000), gcc-sm6115.h has GCC_VENUS_GDSC/GCC_VCODEC0_GDSC and the GCC_VIDEO_* clocks, interconnect sm6115.h has MASTER_VIDEO_P0 and SLAVE_VENUS_CFG, mmnrt_virt exists. agatti.dtsi node: reg 0x5a00000, GIC_SPI 225, iommus 0x860/0x880. Signed firmware qcom/sm6115/Fxtec/QX1050/venus.mbn is in firmware-fxtec-qx1050. Not attempted.
video.source: kernel source 8cd9520; Konrad Dybcio, Venus QoL series v4 (LKML 2023-05, names SM6115/QCM2290 AR50 Lite); Jorge Ramirez-Ortiz, QCM2290 AR50 Lite series v7 (2025-07)

keyboard.title: Keyboard backlight is an on/off GPIO LED; the slider is SW_KEYPAD_SLIDE on gpio-keys, 1 = slid out
keyboard.general: On sliders the keyboard backlight and the slide switch are separate devices: an LED class device and an EV_SW switch. Drive the LED from the switch and the panel state. The DRM connector sysfs dpms attribute follows the compositor output power (atomic ACTIVE) and is a cached value, so it is a safe panel-state source on DSI video-mode panels where backlight actual_brightness reads wedge the link.
keyboard.instance: Pro¹x, linux-pro1x 7.1.0: /sys/class/leds/white:kbd_backlight, max_brightness 1, off at boot. gpio-keys (udev symlink /dev/input/pro1x-slider): type 5 code 10, slide in 0, slide out 1. /sys/class/drm/card0-DSI-1/dpms read Off with sway output power off and On after swaymsg output DSI-1 power on.
keyboard.source: event logger on /dev/input/pro1x-slider with the author sliding; swaymsg -t get_outputs vs dpms; echo 1 > brightness lit the keys (author)

audio.title: A sensor-stack crash on the ADSP takes audio down with it
audio.general: On Qualcomm SoCs the sensor core (SSC) and audio (q6afe/q6asm) share the ADSP. If the sensor core crashes during its init, the ADSP restarts and audio calls fail afterwards: AFE set params timeouts, the codec cannot get its clock, every PCM open fails with EBUSY. Check dmesg for 'fatal error received ... sensor_process' before debugging the audio stack.
audio.instance: Pro1X, Linux 7.1: 'fatal error received: err_qdi.c ... sensor_process ... SNS_REG_INIT ... sns_registry_sensor.c' at 12 s, then 'qcom-q6afe ... AFE set params failed -110', 'va_macro: unable to prepare mclk', wcd937x 'ASoC error (-16)', PipeWire only Dummy Output. Cause: hexagonrpcd da7a374 refused the sensor core's registry writes; 40e5041 accepts them and the crash is gone. SailfishOS's card re-probe (rmmod/modprobe snd_soc_sm8250) made it worse here: the card failed to instantiate until reboot.
audio.source: dmesg on the phone 2026-10-29; hexagonrpc source diff da7a374..40e5041 (apps_std_open_mode); commit 3305bd0

audio.title: The speaker amplifiers are fed by the codec's headphone stage: its gain sets speaker loudness
audio.general: On wcd937x boards with external speaker amplifiers driven from HPH, the HPH volume control decides how loud the speaker gets; a UCM default chosen for headphones leaves the speaker quiet even at 100% software volume.
audio.instance: Pro1X: HPHL/HPHR Volume 0..20 (higher is louder here, not inverted), UCM boot value 12. Author's listening test: 16 louder, 20 wanted for the speaker. Set to 20 in the Speaker devices of HiFi and Voice Call, 12 restored on disable so headphones and earpiece keep 12. The amixer dB scale shown for HPH (0.07 dB steps) is not meaningful.
audio.source: amixer on the phone; author 2026-10-29/30; commit 34eb12f

audio.title: S24_LE playback is about 40 dB too quiet on this card
audio.general: If a card plays far too quietly through the sound server but normally through aplay, compare the sample formats: the server may pick a format the codec path mishandles.
audio.instance: Pro1X: PipeWire opened hw:0,0 as S24_LE (hw_params); the NixOS port forces S16LE with a WirePlumber rule. Confirmed here: barely audible at full volume until the rule applied.

audio.title: Speaker amplifier switches found on with no session running; pops at login
audio.general: Pops when a sound server starts usually mean an amplifier is live while routes change. Read the amplifier switches while nothing plays before blaming the codec.
audio.instance: Pro1X, 2026-10-30: logged out, Spk0/Spk1 OUT Switch and HPHL Switch on although the Speaker DisableSequence ran (HPH gain back to 12). Spk0 went on again seconds after being switched off with no session running (cause unknown). At login PipeWire probes the Voice Call profile (VoiceMMode1 routes on/off for 0.6 s) and then enables HiFi Speaker; the author hears pops at login only. 'amixer events' lists 1279 controls for about a minute before reporting changes. moWerk reports pops at amp power changes, NixOS too.
audio.source: amixer cget/events on the phone; author 2026-10-30

audio.title: Login pops: the PipeWire probe opens the playback PCM repeatedly and each open powers the speaker amplifiers when their switches are left on
audio.general: On ASoC cards whose speaker amplifiers are DAPM widgets behind a mixer switch, a PCM open alone powers the whole path, amplifiers included, if the switch is on. WirePlumber/ACP opens and closes each PCM several times while it probes profiles at startup, so a switch left on by the previous session gives one amplifier power cycle per open: audible pops at every login. Turn the switches off before the audio daemon starts and let the UCM EnableSequence turn them on after the probe. Without ftrace, polling the DAPM debugfs widget files (/sys/kernel/debug/asoc/<card>/<component>/dapm/<widget>) every 10 ms together with /proc/asound/card*/pcm*/sub0/status gives a usable power timeline.
audio.instance: Pro1x, two aw87339 amplifiers (aw87339.1-0059/005a, widgets Spk0/Spk1 SPK PA) fed by the wcd937x HPH stage; controls Spk0/Spk1 OUT Switch. Restarting the Sway session PipeWire 1.6.8 + WirePlumber 0.5.17 by hand (generation 29): with the switches on, pcm0p opened about 8 times in 1.2 s and both amps plus HPHL/HPHR PGA were on from +0.57 s to +1.75 s, with one full off/on cycle. With both switches set to 0 first: 24 probe opens, amps never on; WirePlumber set the switches back on at +1.9 s (Speaker EnableSequence). Fix in pro1x-audio-session (amixer before pipewire). The kernel has no tracefs.
audio.source: DAPM/PCM logs /root/pops/082612 and the AMPS_OFF run on the phone; commit 2624e73, generation 30; the author no longer hears the pops (2026-10-30)

audio.title: A q6voice session does not survive its codec DMA port stopping
audio.general: The hostless voice PCM stays PREPARED, so another front end must keep the back end started. If that stream closes during a call (a card profile switch does), the other side stays silent even after the port and mixer are back; closing and reopening the voice PCM brings the sound back. Open the voice PCM after the keep-alive streams run.
audio.instance: Pro1x, 7.3.0, generations 216-217, 2026-11-04. #216: speaker on cut the sound, speaker off did not restore it, mixer identical. #217 restarts pro1x-voicepcm around the switch: earpiece, speaker and back all had sound both ways (author). The stopped port as the mechanism is inferred; the symptom and the cure are confirmed. The one silent call in #216 was the first after a boot, with pro1x-voicepcm powering the codec before the keep-alive stream; in #217's first call after a boot PipeWire did that and there was sound: two calls.
audio.source: device/audio/pro1x-voice-call; author's test calls; call-audio log

audio.title: Calls have no microphone processing on the phone: TX topology is NONE
audio.general: The q6voice driver's voice TX topology control decides whether the DSP runs echo and noise reduction on the uplink. VSS_IVOCPROC_TOPOLOGY_ID_NONE means none. Noise or echo behaviour heard on the far end then comes from outside the phone's DSP chain.
audio.instance: Pro1x, 7.3.0: 'VoiceMMode1 TX Topology' = 69488 (0x10F70, NONE), RX = 69495 (0x10F77, default). TX_SM_ECNS is 0x10F71, not tried; it may need calibration. Whether the modem processes the uplink further is not known. Tried on 2026-11-04, generation 218: TX topology set to TX_SM_ECNS (69489) by mixer before a call: no error, downlink fine, the far end heard nothing, in two calls; back on NONE the far end hears the phone. No calibration data exists in this port, the NixOS port or the SailfishOS port, and the driver has no way to send any; that this is why is inferred.

sensors.title: SSC sensors need an SSC-enabled iio-sensor-proxy, not just hexagonrpcd
sensors.general: With the sensor core running (QRTR service 400), iio-sensor-proxy still exits if it was built without libssc; it finds no IIO sensor. Check the build option before the DSP side.
sensors.instance: Pro1X: iio-sensor-proxy 3.9 -Dssc-support=enabled with libssc 0.4.4; monitor-sensor: 'Has accelerometer (orientation: undefined, tilt: face-up)' lying flat. The firmware mount matrix is all zeros for every SSC sensor ('falling back to identity'); the udev ACCEL_MOUNT_MATRIX from the NixOS port applies to the accelerometer.
sensors.source: monitor-sensor and iio-sensor-proxy log on the phone; commit e4051eb

sensors.title: ADSP 'Handover signaled, but it already happened' repeats with every SSC sensor batch
sensors.general: On qcom PAS remoteprocs the handover SMP2P bit is meant to rise once at start; the q6v5 driver logs an error for each later rising edge. A streaming sensor client on an SSC (sensors on the ADSP) makes the ADSP raise its ready and handover bits again with each batch, so a running accelerometer stream floods the kernel log; count the smp2p and q6v5 lines in /proc/interrupts over 10 s with and without the client before suspecting a crash.
sensors.instance: Pro1x, kernel 7.1.0 (sm6115-mainline 8cd9520d), generation 33: smp2p-adsp, q6v5 ready and q6v5 handover 43-44 per 10 s with monitor-sensor --accel (iio-sensor-proxy 3.9, libssc) running, 0 without; wdog and fatal 0; ADSP stays up and audio keeps working. Started at the first login, when sway-autorotate started monitor-sensor.
sensors.source: /proc/interrupts on the phone; drivers/remoteproc/qcom_q6v5.c q6v5_handover_interrupt; arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/sm6115.dtsi remoteproc@a400000 interrupts

camera.title: IMX582 exposure capped at one frame of the minimum blanking: libcamera's simple pipeline never raises VBLANK
camera.general: With the software ISP (simple pipeline), libcamera takes the exposure range from the sensor's V4L2 controls at configure time and never writes V4L2_CID_VBLANK, so the longest exposure is the mode's minimum frame length. Dark scenes and indoor photos come out underexposed whatever the AE or a manual exposure asks. Pipelines that handle this (Raspberry Pi, rkisp1) raise VBLANK with the exposure.
camera.instance: Pro1x, IMX582 1984x1080 mode (pro1x-imx582-1080p), kernel 7.1 (3nfp9v97), libcamera-pro1x 0.7.2, 2026-11-02: subdev /dev/v4l-subdev19, vertical_blanking min 70 max 64420 (default and in use 70), hblank 1056, pixel rate 321.6 MHz, so 9.45 us a line; exposure max 1102 lines = 10416 us. Asked 30000 and 100000 us (manual) or auto in the dark: applied 10416 us every time (auto: gain 16, mean 0.2/255). Setting vertical_blanking=2120 by hand raises the sensor's exposure max to 3000-3152 lines, kept during streaming, but libcamera still applied 1102 lines. Up to ~0.6 s would be possible at the maximum blanking. Fixed by our libcamera patch 0018 (VBLANK raised per frame, priority delayed control): applied exposures 29993, 99991, 299992 us for 30, 100, 300 ms asked; 0.9 s asked gives 618700 us (blanking maximum, 65452 lines); 8 frames at 300 ms took 2.1 s; auto now up to 6982 lines (66 ms). Tested on the phone with the patched libcamera, not yet deployed.
camera.source: headless libcamerasrc test (agent's camtest.py through the camera app's environment), v4l2-ctl on the subdev; libcamera src/ipa/simple/soft_simple.cpp configure() takes exposureMax from configInfo.sensorControls

camera.title: A flash LED in the sensor's flash-leds, without V4L2 flash support, can leave a camera without media links
camera.general: When a device tree links a flash LED to a sensor, camss's async notifier may wait for a V4L2 flash subdevice. Without the kernel option that subdevice never registers. Check for 0 links in media-ctl first, then compare the config with a working port.
camera.instance: Pro1x, 7.3.0, patch 0027 flash-leds on the rear camera; imx582 and s5k4h7 present with 0 links, libcamera reports no camera, CONFIG_V4L2_FLASH_LED_CLASS not set although LEDS_CLASS_FLASH and LEDS_QCOM_FLASH are =m. moWerk's sfos.fragment sets it =m; it was the only camera-related difference found between his fragment and our config. Booted 2026-11-04 (generation 210): both sensors have links, white:flash-0 and dw9800 are entities, cam -l lists back and front, and the author reports the camera app more or less works. The notifier wait itself was not traced.
camera.confidence: confirmed that the option fixes it; mechanism inferred
camera.source: media-ctl and cam -l on the phone; moWerk kernel/sfos.fragment:70 and HANDOVER.md; device/kernel/pro1x-7.3.fragment

haptics.title: AW86224: the stock waveform file holds plain sine bursts
haptics.general: Before seeking a vendor's haptic blob, decode it: this one is a table of start and end addresses and full-amplitude sines, which a free driver can generate. The vendor's sharper feel likely comes from playing from chip memory rather than continuous drive.
haptics.instance: aw8622x_haptic.bin (1222 bytes, TheMuppets vendor repo): 2-byte checksum, base address 0, version 0x55, waves of 330, 809 and 59 samples, 60 samples per cycle (200 Hz at the driver's 12 kHz). LineageOS aw8622x.c uses wave 2 for short effects, a looped long wave otherwise. Not tried on the phone yet.
haptics.confidence: confirmed for the file and driver source; the feel is inferred
